guide_enrichment.narrative:
What stands out to us is Ole Miss’ ability to create scoring opportunities against a Florida defense that has struggled to prevent them. The Rebels have also shown multiple ways to move the ball: Trinidad Chambliss produced 561 passing yards and five touchdowns through two games, while Kewan Lacy added 148 rushing yards and three scores. Ole Miss played at one of the nation’s fastest early-season paces and converted every red-zone possession over that stretch. We are not treating two games as proof, but that profile supports the offensive advantages in our longer-run numbers.

The counterweight is an Ole Miss defense that allowed 395.5 yards per game through two contests, even while holding opponents to a 33.3 percent third-down conversion rate. Our numbers favor that defense in preventing Florida from consistently creating scoring opportunities, but the overall matchup still leaves limited separation from the market. For us, the pass is about price: the available improvement comes with additional cost, and the football case is not strong enough to create meaningful value.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching the Ole Miss rushing offense against Florida’s run defense. Our numbers identify that as a meaningful advantage, and Lacy’s early production gives the Rebels a proven option alongside Chambliss, who also rushed for 62 yards and a touchdown through two games. If Ole Miss can stay efficient on the ground, its pace becomes more difficult for Florida to manage and its scoring-opportunity edge becomes more relevant. That matchup supports Ole Miss, but not enough for us to force a wager at the available price.

recent_game.fact: Ole Miss defeated Charlotte 41-9 to improve to 2-0.
Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss completed a career-high 88 percent of his passes for 225 yards and two touchdowns against Charlotte.
Running back Kewan Lacy carried 13 times for 87 yards and two touchdowns against Charlotte.
Wide receiver Deuce Alexander caught a career-high eight passes for 76 yards against Charlotte.
Nick Cull made his first interception as an Ole Miss player against Charlotte.

quarterback.fact: Trinidad Chambliss is Ole Miss' starting quarterback, with Deuce Knight or Walker Howard listed as the next options on the depth chart.
Chambliss completed 44 of 62 passes for 561 yards, five touchdowns and one interception through two games.
Chambliss also rushed 12 times for 62 yards and one touchdown through two games.
Chambliss had thrown a touchdown pass in 15 consecutive games, the fourth-longest streak in Ole Miss history.

offensive_personnel.fact: Ole Miss' listed starting offensive line was Terez Davis at left tackle, Delano Townsend at left guard, Brycen Sanders at center, Patrick Kutas at right guard and Tommy Kinsler IV at right tackle.
Connor Howes was listed behind Tommy Kinsler IV at right tackle after Kinsler missed the Charlotte game because of injury.
Running back Kewan Lacy had 30 carries for 148 yards and three touchdowns through two games.
Lacy had scored a rushing touchdown in 11 consecutive games, the second-longest active streak in the FBS.
Wide receiver Deuce Alexander led Ole Miss through two games with 13 receptions for 235 yards and two touchdowns.

Transfers Johntay Cook II and Horatio Fields were listed as starting receivers; Cook had two catches for 12 yards and a touchdown, while Fields had nine catches for 113 yards and a touchdown through two games.
The tight-end depth chart listed Luke Hasz, Caleb Odom and Michael Smith as co-options.

Five Rebels had made their first career starts during the first two games: wide receiver Deuce Alexander, defensive tackle Jamarious Brown, offensive linemen Connor Howes and Tommy Kinsler IV, and safety Anthony Robinson III.

defensive_personnel.fact: The listed defensive front consisted of Kam Franklin at defensive end, Jamarious Brown at nose tackle, Will Echoles at defensive tackle and Suntarine Perkins or Blake Purchase at edge.
Transfer linebackers Keaton Thomas and Luke Ferrelli were listed as starters; each had 12 and 11 tackles, respectively, through two games.
Ferrelli led Ole Miss with six tackles against Charlotte and had 11 tackles and one sack through two games.
Cornerback Jaylon Braxton had 11 tackles and three pass breakups through two games, including two breakups against Charlotte.

The listed secondary starters were Jaylon Braxton at one corner, Antonio Kite or Jalyn Crawford at the other corner, Edwin Joseph at nickel, Joenel Aguero at free safety, and Sharif Denson or Anthony Robinson III at strong safety.

coaching_changes.fact: Pete Golding is in his first full season as Ole Miss head coach after being named to the position on Nov. 30, 2025; he previously spent three seasons as the Rebels' defensive coordinator.

John David Baker is the new offensive coordinator and calls the offense from the coaches' booth; he returned after serving as East Carolina's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach from 2024-25.
Bryan Brown is the new defensive coordinator and works from the coaches' booth after serving the previous two seasons as Ole Miss' co-defensive coordinator and secondary coach.
John Garrison serves as offensive line and run game coordinator, while Joe Judge serves as head coach of offense and quarterbacks coach.

injury_availability.fact: Tight end Caleb Odom missed the Charlotte game because of injury.
Right tackle Tommy Kinsler IV missed the Charlotte game because of injury.

offensive_context.fact: Ole Miss averaged 41.0 points, 454.0 total yards, 314.5 passing yards and 139.5 rushing yards per game through two games.
The Rebels had scored on every red-zone possession through two games and had allowed 0.5 sacks per game.
Ole Miss ranked fifth nationally in pace at 22.7 seconds per play through two games.

defensive_context.fact: Ole Miss allowed 23.5 points and 395.5 total yards per game through two games, including 152.5 rushing yards and 243.0 passing yards per game.
The defense averaged seven tackles for loss and two sacks per game through two games.
Ole Miss held opponents to a 33.3 percent conversion rate on third down through two games.

special_teams.fact: Kicker Lucas Carneiro was 4-for-5 on field goals and 10-for-10 on extra points through two games.
Carneiro made both field-goal attempts against Charlotte, including a season-long 57-yarder.
Carneiro had made six field goals of at least 50 yards since joining Ole Miss in 2025, a program career record.
Punter Oscar Bird averaged 45.4 yards on five punts through two games.
Deuce Alexander or Traylon Ray were listed as Ole Miss' options at both kickoff returner and punt returner.

Ole Miss entered Game 3 with a 2-0 record and was ranked No. 8 in the AP poll and No. 9 in the Coaches poll.
